Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'inspect' returns the accessibility tree of the front app (what a screen reader reads, which can differ from what is drawn) as JSON — per element: type, label, value, frame [x,y,width,height] in device points from the top-left, traits the type does not imply, enabled only when false, children. Call 'inspect' before a 'tap' on anything you have not located in this screen's tree, before answering what text a screen shows, and before reporting a control's state (a switch's value, whether a button is enabled, which tab is selected) or whether a sheet, alert or other modal is in front (the result says so) — never guess coordinates from memory of similar apps, and do not 'screenshot' for these. Go straight to 'screenshot' for color, images, and layout. Three reads: no marker and no x/y = the whole visible tree (the safe default when you do not know the exact label); marker = the first element, in tree order, whose label contains that CASE-SENSITIVE substring — a title can match before the button with the same text, so check the matched element's type; x/y = the element drawn on top at that point, as a tap would find it, with its descendants (a point between controls hits their container). If a marker misses or returns the wrong element, read the whole tree instead of guessing or screenshotting. Then tap the center of the target's frame. Hidden, off-screen, and illegibly small elements are omitted and counted; text longer than its area shows is cut (it ends with ...). Only the x/y read resolves occlusion, and only by bars and containers it can recognize: a frame from the whole-tree or marker read that overlaps a later sibling (a tab bar, a sheet) may be covered, so before tapping it read x/y at its center; a point on a sheet's blank area can still read the content behind it, so when the result reports a modal, stay inside it. A tree over the size cap loses its deepest levels first and says so — narrow with marker, or with x/y on the target itself: a point in a gap answers the container around it, which is no smaller; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

## A5. What the two guard suites enforce

### `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts` (129 lines)

Exists — at the path you gave. **Scope:** walks `overrides/app/components/**` for every `*.css.ts` that declares a `parts: [...]` array (single-part recipes are skipped), then reads the **sibling `index.tsx`** in the same directory.

Enforces:
1. **Every part the component reads off `styles` must be declared in `parts`.** Regex `READ_RE = /\bstyles(?:\.([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*)|\[\s*'([^']+)'\s*\])/g` matches `styles.foo` and `styles['foo']`. Rationale in the header: `parts` gates `variants`/`sizes` but **not** `baseStyle`, so an undeclared part renders fine today and silently stops responding the day a variant is added.
2. **A sibling `index.tsx` must exist** next to every multipart recipe (`componentFound` must be `true`).
3. **Vacuity guard** — the walk must collect something, every collected recipe must have `declared.length > 0`, and at least one must have `read.length > 0`.

Practical consequence for a new recipe: if it's multipart, it **must** live at `<dir>/<name>.css.ts` beside an `index.tsx`, and `parts` must be a superset of every `styles.X` read in that `index.tsx`. `//` line comments are stripped before both regexes run, so commented-out `styles.foo` won't false-positive, and inline comments inside the `parts` array are tolerated.

### `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts` (375 lines)

Exists. **Scope:** walks the registered map — `components` from `./index` plus the composed `theme` — so **anything you add to `index.ts` is immediately under these five assertions.** It resolves function-form `baseStyle` across **all 2^5 = 32 boolean prop combinations** (`inverse`, `disabled`, `hasError`, `focused`, `filled`), plus `variants` and `sizes`.

Six tests:
1. `collect() actually walks the registered recipes` — vacuity guard; `Object.keys(components).length > 0` and `collect().length > 0`.
2. **No sizing property uses a bare spacing-scale key.** `SIZING_PROPS` (`width`/`height`/`minW`/`maxW`/`boxSize`/…) × spacing keys → banned. `width: 'xl'` reads Chakra's `sizes.xl` (36rem), not `space.xl`.
3. **No typography property uses a bare scale key.** `fontSize`/`lineHeight`/`letterSpacing` against (own Zimmermann scale keys ∪ spacing keys). Use `textStyle` or `var(--zimm-font-*)`. `fontWeight` deliberately exempt.
4. **No compound shorthand contains a bare scale key.** `padding`/`margin`/`inset`/`gap`/`p`/`m` with a space in the value; `var(...)` is masked out first. `padding: 'xs 0'` is emitted verbatim and dropped by the browser.
5. **House style: no bare token key on a registered scale.** `SPACE_PROPS` × spacing keys, and `COLOR_PROPS` × flattened `colour.ts` keys (dot-paths like `text.default`, `action.primary.bgDefault`) → must use `var(--zimm-scale-*)` / `var(--zimm-color-*)`.
6. **No recipe silently inherits a base SFCC recipe of the same name.** `extendTheme` deep-merges, so any key name that collides with a base recipe inherits it. Allowlist is hardcoded:
   ```js
   const INTENTIONAL_MERGES = ['Button', 'Header', 'ListMenu'];
   ```
   **This is the hard constraint on naming a new recipe key: it must be `Zimm`-prefixed (or otherwise not collide with a base SFCC recipe name), or the test fails.** Adding a 4th intentional merge requires editing this array.

Known blind spots documented in the header (both suites are theme/sibling walks, not JSX-attribute scanners): a live failure of mode 2 at `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx:302` (`fontSize="l"`, emits nothing) is unreachable by either suite.
